gloss: traditional boys' school uniform with stand-up collar

definitions.gloss: traditional boys' school uniform with stand-up collar
definitions.explanation: A black, military-style uniform with a stand-up collar (Prussian collar) and brass buttons, traditionally worn by male students in Japanese middle and high schools. Still used at many schools today.

examples.japanese: {学|がく}ラン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}た→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧。
examples.english: A boy wearing a gakuran uniform.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中学校|ちゅうがっこう}→中学校：01465_chuugakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{制服|せいふく}→制服：03086_seifuku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{学|がく}ランだった。
examples.english: The uniform at my middle school was a gakuran.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ブレザー→ブレザー：28533_burezaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えて→増える：01183_fueru⟧、{学|がく}ラン⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{少|すく}なく→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, schools with blazers have increased and gakuran uniforms have become less common.

notes:
{学|がく}ラン comes from ⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧ (⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧, student) + ラン (from the Dutch word "rand" or the Japanese abbreviation of オランダ, referring to Western-style clothing).

The {学|がく}ラン is characterized by:
- ⟦{詰|つ}め{襟|えり}→詰め襟：14588_tsumeeri⟧ (stand-up collar)
- ⟦{黒|くろ}→黒：02205_kuro⟧ or ⟦{紺|こん}→紺：03885_kon⟧ color
- {金|きん}⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧ (brass buttons)

The female counterpart is the ⟦セーラー{服|ふく}→セーラー服：17677_seeraafuku⟧ (sailor uniform). Both are iconic symbols of Japanese school life, though many schools have switched to ⟦ブレザー→ブレザー：28533_burezaa⟧ (blazer) style uniforms.
